source: English translation of bosla_paths_guide.docx (the Arabic original is the reference)
notes: Certifications: the listed professional certifications are paid unless stated otherwise, and are shown separately from free learning resources.
Fees and information are up to date as of November 2026 and may change. Always confirm on the official website of the issuing body.
Sticking to the guide: the agent does not suggest any certification or resource that is not in this guide.
Free resources: admission to free resources may depend on cohorts or announced conditions.

paths.description: Collects, cleans and analyzes data, then turns it into reports and dashboards that help management make decisions.
tasks: Extracting data from databases.
Cleaning data and handling errors and missing values.
Preparing reports and KPI dashboards.
Presenting findings and recommendations to decision makers.
skills: A data visualization tool: Power BI or Tableau
paths.traits: Loves numbers, patient with details, and curious about why things happen.

certifications.name: Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate
certifications.details: A beginner certificate on Coursera, about 6 months at 10 hours a week, covering data cleaning, analysis and visualization with tools such as spreadsheets, SQL, Python and Tableau.

certifications.name: Microsoft PL-300 (Power BI Data Analyst Associate)
certifications.details: An intermediate certificate with no prerequisites, focused on Power Query and DAX. The exam fee is about 165 USD and may vary by country.

freeResources.name: Tuwaiq Academy
freeResources.details: Data analysis bootcamp covering Excel, SQL, Power BI, Tableau and Python; admission is by cohort.

freeResources.name: Satr platform
freeResources.details: A free data analysis track that starts with programming and database basics, then data analysis with Python libraries.

freeResources.name: Microsoft Learn
freeResources.details: A free learning path to prepare for the PL-300 exam.

beginner.text: Advanced Excel and statistics basics
SQL, then Power BI
A small analytics project for your portfolio

advanced.text: Advanced SQL
Power BI and preparing for the PL-300 exam
3 portfolio projects and applying for an internship or job

interview: How do you handle data that has missing values?
What is the difference between INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN?
Describe an analysis you did and how it supported a decision.

paths.description: Designs and builds the reporting systems and KPI dashboards that senior management relies on. Focuses on building data models and their quality more than interpreting them; they "build the platform" that analysts and managers use.
tasks: Building data models and connecting their sources.
Setting up data extraction, transformation and loading (ETL) processes.
Designing KPI dashboards for management.
Ensuring data accuracy and managing access permissions.
paths.traits: Loves building and organizing, precise, and cares that things look clear and easy to read.

certifications.name: Microsoft PL-300 (Power BI Data Analyst Associate)
certifications.details: An intermediate certificate with no prerequisites, focused on Power Query, DAX and data modeling. The exam fee is about 165 USD and may vary by country.

freeResources.name: Satr platform
freeResources.details: Business intelligence track with 9 courses focused on data analysis and visualization.

freeResources.name: Tuwaiq Academy
freeResources.details: Data management and analysis program using Microsoft SQL Server; admission is by cohort.

freeResources.name: Microsoft Learn
freeResources.details: A free learning path to prepare for the PL-300 exam.

beginner.text: Excel, database basics and SQL
Power BI and data modeling
A complete KPI dashboard for a fictional company

advanced.text: Advanced SQL and ETL concepts
Advanced DAX and preparing for the PL-300 exam
3 portfolio dashboards and applying for an internship or job

interview: What is the difference between a Fact table and a Dimension table?
How do you choose the right KPIs for a dashboard aimed at senior management?
If you have a slow dashboard, how would you improve its performance?

paths.description: The link between management and the technical team. Understands business needs and turns them into clear requirements the technical team builds the solution on, and suggests process improvements.
tasks: Holding interviews and workshops with stakeholders to gather requirements.
Documenting requirements and writing User Stories.
Mapping current and future processes using BPMN.
Following up on solution delivery and taking part in user acceptance testing.
skills: Tools such as Jira and Visio
paths.traits: A good listener, curious, and enjoys solving problems together with people.

certifications.name: ECBA by IIBA
certifications.details: An entry-level business analysis certificate that requires no prior experience. The fee is 395 USD and includes one year of IIBA membership; discounted student prices are available.

freeResources.name: Doroob platform
freeResources.details: Courses in business administration and job skills; some are free.

freeResources.name: Self-practice
freeResources.details: Pick a real process at your university (such as course registration), document it, map it and suggest an improvement; this is the best free hands-on training.

beginner.text: Business analysis basics and getting to know the BABOK guide
Process mapping with BPMN, requirements documentation and Excel
Case study: analyze a university process and suggest an improvement

advanced.text: Preparing for the ECBA exam
SQL basics and Jira, then the ECBA exam
Two portfolio case studies and applying for an internship or job

interview: How do you deal with a stakeholder whose requirements keep changing?
What is the difference between functional and non-functional requirements?
Describe a process you analyzed or improved, and what was the outcome?

paths.description: Sets information security policies and procedures, assesses risks, and makes sure the organization complies with regulations and standards. It is the closest security path for an MIS student because it combines technology and management.
tasks: Writing and reviewing security policies.
Assessing risks and preparing the risk register.
Auditing compliance with security controls.
Raising security awareness among employees.
skills: Understanding frameworks and controls such as ISO 27001 and the Essential Cybersecurity Controls (ECC) issued by the National Cybersecurity Authority
paths.traits: Precise, likes regulations and compliance, and can persuade others without conflict.

certifications.name: ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity (CC)
certifications.details: An entry-level cybersecurity certificate. Note: the ISC2 program that offered it for free (One Million Certified in Cybersecurity) has ended, so it is now treated as a paid certificate, and students should check its fee on the ISC2 website.

freeResources.name: Tuwaiq Academy
freeResources.details: The "Tuwaiq Cyber" bootcamp and cybersecurity fundamentals programs; admission is by cohort.

freeResources.name: Doroob platform
freeResources.details: Information security courses; some are free.

beginner.text: Networking and cybersecurity basics
Concepts of risks, policies and controls
Project: a simple security policy and a risk assessment for a fictional organization

advanced.text: Preparing for the CC certificate
The CC exam and studying a national controls framework
Two portfolio risk assessment projects and applying for an internship or job

interview: What is the difference between a risk, a threat and a vulnerability?
How would you convince management to adopt a security policy they see as complicated?
What are the components of a risk register?

paths.description: Plans technical projects, coordinates team members, and follows up on execution until the project is delivered within the agreed time, budget and scope.
tasks: Preparing the project plan and schedule.
Managing risks and change requests.
Coordinating between teams and stakeholders.
Preparing project progress reports.
skills: Project management basics with both traditional and Agile/Scrum approaches
Tools such as MS Project, Jira and Trello
paths.traits: A leader, organized, and calm under pressure.

certifications.name: CAPM by PMI
certifications.details: Requires no work experience; requires a secondary school diploma and 23 hours of project management education. The exam fee is 225 USD for PMI members and 300 USD for non-members, and the exam is available in Arabic.

freeResources.name: Doroob platform
freeResources.details: Project management track with 8 free courses.

freeResources.name: The Scrum Guide
freeResources.details: The official guide to the Scrum framework, available for free.

beginner.text: Project management basics and the Doroob track
Agile, Scrum and Trello or Jira
Managing a small real project (a club or an event) and documenting it

advanced.text: Completing 23 hours of project management education
Preparing for the CAPM exam, then taking it
A portfolio case study and applying for an internship or job

interview: If your project falls behind schedule, what do you do?
What is the difference between Waterfall and Agile, and when do you use each?
How do you deal with a team member who does not deliver their tasks?

paths.description: Implements enterprise resource planning systems such as SAP and Oracle, and configures them to fit the organization's processes in finance, procurement, inventory and human resources.
tasks: Analyzing the client's current processes.
Configuring the system.
Migrating data into the system and testing it.
Training users and supporting them after go-live.
skills: Understanding business processes: finance, supply chain and procurement
Mastering at least one ERP system
paths.traits: Likes understanding how companies work from the inside, patient, and precise.

certifications.name: SAP Certified Associate
certifications.details: Multiple certificates by module (such as finance or procurement). Preparation is free through learning journeys, while exam attempts are purchased.

freeResources.name: SAP Learning (learning journeys)
freeResources.details: Free SAP learning journeys that prepare for the certificates and cover many topics.

freeResources.name: Doroob platform
freeResources.details: Accounting and finance courses that help you understand the processes the system covers; some are free.

beginner.text: Business process basics: accounting, procurement and inventory
An introductory SAP learning journey
Project: map the "Procure-to-Pay" cycle and link it to the system modules

advanced.text: Choosing a module (finance or procurement) and a learning journey that qualifies for its certificate
Preparing for the certificate exam, then taking it
Applying for an internship with an ERP implementation partner

interview: What is an ERP system, and how does it benefit an organization?
Explain the "Procure-to-Pay" cycle.
How do you deal with users who resist a new system?

paths.description: Helps organizations improve their processes and services using technology: diagnoses the current state, proposes solutions, and leads change within the organization.
tasks: Assessing the organization's digital maturity level.
Identifying opportunities to automate manual processes.
Preparing a digital transformation roadmap.
Managing change and preparing employees for new systems.
skills: Knowledge of modern technologies: cloud, automation and artificial intelligence
paths.traits: A visionary, persuasive, and loves renewal.

certifications.name: ITIL 4 Foundation
certifications.details: An entry-level IT service management certificate offered by PeopleCert, and a suitable start for those working in digital transformation.

freeResources.name: Doroob platform
freeResources.details: Courses in business administration and leadership; some are free.

freeResources.name: Microsoft Learn
freeResources.details: Free learning paths in cloud fundamentals, artificial intelligence and process automation.

beginner.text: Digital transformation concepts and digital maturity models
Cloud basics and process automation (such as Power Automate)
Project: a simple digital transformation plan for a small business

advanced.text: Preparing for the ITIL 4 Foundation certificate
The ITIL exam and automating a real process
Two portfolio case studies and applying to graduate programs at consulting firms

interview: How do you measure the success of a digital transformation project?
If the organization resists change, where do you start?
Give an example of a manual process that could be automated, and how?

paths.description: Leads the development of a digital product (an app or a platform) from understanding user needs to launch and continuous improvement, and decides what gets built first.
tasks: Conducting user research and market analysis.
Writing the product roadmap and setting its priorities.
Working daily with designers and developers.
Tracking product usage metrics and making improvement decisions.
paths.traits: Creative, a leader even without direct authority, and passionate about digital products.

certifications.name: PSPO I by Scrum.org
certifications.details: The Product Owner certificate in the Scrum framework. No course attendance is required, the exam fee is 200 USD, and it is valid for life without renewal.

freeResources.name: The Scrum Guide
freeResources.details: The official guide to the Scrum framework, available for free.

freeResources.name: Tuwaiq Academy
freeResources.details: UX/UI design bootcamp; admission is by cohort.

beginner.text: Product management and user experience basics
Scrum and Figma
Project: an app idea with user research, a prototype and a roadmap

advanced.text: Preparing for the PSPO I exam
The PSPO I exam, plus analyzing an existing product and suggesting an improvement
A portfolio with two products and applying for an internship or job

interview: How do you decide which feature gets built first?
Pick an app you use and suggest an improvement to it.
What is the difference between a Product Owner and a Project Manager?
